extracted.intended_audience: innovators, inventors, makers, and others using patent data for intelligence
extracted.subtask_description: Describe the parts of a patent document and the kinds of data contained on-page and off-page that are useful for patent intelligence. Focus is on what to look for (front page fields, drawings, description, claims) and additional metadata that informs analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Type (front page)
rubrics_metrics.description: The front page includes a variety of information, including the title and abstract, but even more basic, the document type. There are published patent applications and issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the record is a published application or an issued/granted patent via the top-of-page indicators and the kind code (the last two characters of the publication number) which defines more nuanced document types. Both applications and granted patents are useful for intelligence; note that granted patents can differ from their original applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geography / Patenting Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Also at the top of the page, you can see the patenting authority or country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first two characters of the publication number is the two-letter country or authority code; use this to identify jurisdictional scope and authority-specific conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates (publication, filing, priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a granted patent, there is the publication date, which is when the patent issued, and there are a couple additional dates for filing and priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each date carries meaning for analysis (e.g., priority determines prior art date, filing dates track prosecution timeline); use the appropriate date for the analysis task (timeline, novelty window, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The title is straight forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles are not unique and can be vague; do not rely on title alone for identification or to infer scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract is a short summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for a quick high-level understanding, but not authoritative for determining claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: On the front page is a representative drawing, selected by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title, abstract, and front page drawing together provide a simple summary but are not the source for determining what the patent actually covers; always consult claims and full disclosure for scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventors and their city of residence
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors and their city of residence. Anyone who has contributed to the invention should be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first inventor is called out at the top of the US patent and may be significant, but some listings may be alphabetical or otherwise non-significant. Use inventor names and locations for affiliation/assignee inference, inventor collaboration networks, and provenance checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignees (owner at time of issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees shows the owner of the patent at the time of issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The face of the patent reflects the original assignee; current owner may differ. For corporate ownership and freedom-to-operate or competitor mapping, check assignment records and post-issuance transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification codes, which come from hierarchical technical classification systems assigned by the patent offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These codes map to descriptions of technical categories and are useful for topic/technology grouping, searching, and analytics across portfolios and authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of references / cited prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of references or cited prior art – this is a list of the considered prior art during the examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the examiner cited these references during prosecution, they indicate what the examiner considered and that the examiner determined the invention was patentable over them; use cited art for prior-art landscaping and prosecution context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties involved in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Lastly, the parties involved in the patent prosecution – the examiner(s) and attorney, agent, or firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parties can provide context on prosecution style, firm specialization, and potential contacts for licensing or validity questions; include them when tracking prosecution histories or assessing quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings (presence, types, and reference numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents generally include at least one drawing, which are provided to help understand the invention. There may be multiple views, an exploded view to show the individual elements, and drawings of one or more components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings are an important part of the disclosure; good disclosures include as many drawings as needed to demonstrate the invention. Each element is distinguished with a reference number which is described in the description—use drawings to understand embodiment structure and element mapping to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sections (background, summary, list of drawings, detailed description)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description follows and can be quite lengthy. It is usually broken into sections, and those sections vary between authorities. Usually there is a background section, summary of the invention, list of drawings, and detailed description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background often provides general context but little about the invention; focus on the summary and detailed description for embodiments, alternatives, and implementation details that inform claim interpretation and enablement analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-number naming / element descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings are listed and described, and the little reference numbers that point to each element are named and described in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mapping between reference numbers and element names to tie drawings to written embodiments and to trace element definitions relevant to claim terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement / Technical disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: This makes up main technical disclosure, and as discussed earlier, this is what should enable a person skilled in this field to make or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the description provides sufficient information to enable a person skilled in the art; enablement affects validity and practical implementability and is central for technical assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims (scope definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims set forth and define the scope of the exclusive rights – what the patent covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are the authoritative source of legal scope; use claim language for freedom-to-operate, infringement, and scope mapping rather than relying on title/abstract/drawings alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-page metadata: current assignees and entity metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: There is also metadata not found within these pages - things like the current assignees or owner and metadata on those entities like location or size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrich patent records with external metadata (current ownership, company size, location) to inform competitive intelligence, licensing potential, and market mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated expiry date
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata such as estimated expiry date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filing/priority and term adjustment/maintenance information to compute expiry; expiry affects enforceability and market opportunity windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata such as maintenance payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance/renewal payment records indicate whether a patent is being kept in force and can signal the owner's ongoing interest or abandonment risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed legal events and legal status
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed legal events, legal status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track prosecution events, grants, re-examinations, oppositions, and other status events to understand enforceability, pendency, and lifecycle stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata such as litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation records indicate disputes, potential strength/weakness of a right, and can be critical when assessing risk, validity challenges, or licensing leverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward citations (later patents that cite this patent) can be used as an indicator of technological influence, impact, or relevance; use cautiously alongside other metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: File wrapper / file history (prosecution record)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is also a file wrapper or file history that includes the details of the patent prosecution – back and forth between the patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the file history for arguments, amendments, and examiner reasoning; prosecution history can speak to patent quality and is invaluable backstory if a patent is of key interest by way of threat or opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consistent patent-viewing tools
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the many advantages of using a tool that searches and displays patents from around the world is a consistent patent view to limit reviewing the original patent PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage tools that normalize views across authorities to speed analysis, but verify details (claims, drawings, legal events) against original documents or authoritative records when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: front-page summary not authoritative for scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The title, abstract, and front page drawing together provide a simple summary of the invention, but are not the source for determining what the patent actually covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always rely on claim language (and supporting description) for determining coverage; use front-page elements only for quick triage and initial understanding.
